clue.text: Sweet shot with son wearing black hat

parts.note: a shot is an attempt, a go
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
a topper is a top hat

explanation.surface: Someone fires a shot alongside their son, who is dressed in a black hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The son 'wearing' the black hat is read as B then S beside TOPPER; the pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A gobstopper is a large, very hard round confection, so it is a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Object found in circle, pocketed by girl

indicators.note: something pocketed by another is tucked inside it, so the circle goes within the girl

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
O is a circle by its shape

explanation.surface: A girl finds an object inside a ring and slips it into her pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: An object in the sense of an aim or purpose is a synonym for a target one strives for.

clue.text: Reserve ten, about right for a present perhaps

parts.note: to reserve a table or seat is to book it

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word ten surrounds the letters for right

parts.note: OK means all right, correct

explanation.surface: Someone sets aside ten of something, a sum about right for a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example: a voucher is one kind of present.
explanation.definitionFit: A voucher exchangeable for reading matter is a typical gift, hence an example of a present.

clue.text: Great figure of Italian cast in bronze

indicators.note: something cast in a material is set within it, so Italian is placed inside bronze

parts.note: tan is a bronze colour, as in a suntan
IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in vermouth

explanation.surface: A statue of a great Italian figure has been cast in bronze.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sculpture or the painter Titian; 'cast in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a giant or a person of colossal importance, named after the mythical Greek giants.

clue.text: Country lover quiet at rising

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a rising or uprising is a riot

explanation.surface: A lover of the countryside keeps quiet at an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' looks like a reversal signal in a down clue, but it is a noun meaning an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot is someone devoted to their nation, so a lover of their land.

clue.text: Eastern aquatic bird, on a lake unaffected by time

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: An eastern water bird on a lake seems untouched by the passing years.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting, without beginning or end, is not touched by time's passage.

clue.text: Scene right out of play

indicators.note: taking the letter out of the word means removing it

parts.note: sport is play or amusement

explanation.surface: A scene is cut from a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' suggests theatre beside 'Scene', but here it means fun or games, SPORT; 'out of' removes R.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a place or location, as is a scene in the sense of the site of events.

clue.text: Very good on a revolutionary instrument

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, very good

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the words on a are read backwards

explanation.surface: Something very good is played on a radical new instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns 'on a' round to give ANO.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano is a keyboard instrument with hammers striking strings.

clue.text: Fairy ring sat on by mischievous child

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits on top of the second, which is sat on

parts.note: a tinker is informally a naughty or rascally child
to ring is to bell, and a bell is something that rings

explanation.surface: A naughty child sits on a fairy ring of mushrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'sat on by' puts TINKER above BELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinker Bell is the sprite in J M Barrie's Peter Pan.

clue.text: Dealing with a bishop, exposed …

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
out means revealed, made public

explanation.surface: A news story concerns a bishop whose secret has come out.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition meaning concerning or on the subject of is a synonym of 'dealing with'.

clue.text: .. on the other hand, the knight gets a win

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
to win is to gain

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, the bishop is exposed but the knight wins.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this clue to 9 across, a chess story; the definition is the opening phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a contrasting consideration, an idiom equivalent to 'alternatively'.

clue.text: A sherry in the morning? Approximately two, ultimately, downed

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

indicators.note: something downed is swallowed, so the letter goes inside the phrase

parts.note: or so means approximately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word two

explanation.surface: Someone has downed a couple of sherries in the morning, or so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' picks the final letter of 'two', and 'downed' means swallowed, putting that letter inside the phrase for approximately.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoroso is a sweetened style of oloroso from Jerez, one type of fortified Spanish wine.

clue.text: Isn't one suffering stress?

indicators.note: letters that are suffering are in a bad way and get rearranged

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question: surely anyone suffering is under strain?
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' shuffles the letters of ISN'T ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is mental or physical strain, a synonym of stress.

clue.text: Old region producing gas

parts.note: a zone is a region or area

explanation.surface: An old area is a source of gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen with three atoms per molecule, a pungent gas.

clue.text: Incredible payments must be made to support area, no matter what

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece that supports another sits beneath it, so the area comes first

parts.note: a tall story is an incredible one
costs are payments or charges

explanation.surface: Unbelievable charges must be paid to keep an area going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incredible' looks like an anagram signal but means TALL.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means whatever the price or effort, regardless of anything.

clue.text: Date of surveillance operation leader overlooked

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and overlooking it means dropping it

parts.note: a stakeout is police watching a place covertly

explanation.surface: A date is set for a stakeout, but the man in charge is ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Date' is a verb: to take someone out is to go on a date with them.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone out is to escort them socially, which is what dating someone means.

clue.text: More or less shut up upon greeting jealous husband

indicators.note: in a down answer, upon means the first piece sits above the second
in a down answer, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a door that is to is pushed nearly closed
hello is a greeting

explanation.surface: A man more or less silenced by a greeting turns out to be a jealous husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TO, nearly shut as a door left 'to', giving OT above HELLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Moor murders his wife Desdemona out of sexual jealousy.

clue.text: One may be raised with pride

definitions.text: One may be raised with pride

parts.words: One may be raised with pride
parts.note: a group of lions is a pride, so a youngster is reared within one; the surface suggests a proud flag or child

explanation.surface: Something, perhaps a flag or a child, is lifted or brought up with great pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' is the collective noun for lions, and 'raised' means reared.
explanation.definitionFit: A young lion grows up in its family group, the pride.

clue.text: Tower in settlement above a river

indicators.note: in a down answer, above means the first piece sits on top of the others

parts.note: a camp is a temporary settlement
the Nile is the African river

explanation.surface: A tower stands in a village overlooking a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A campanile is a free-standing bell tower, as at Venice or Pisa.

clue.text: Friendly ball? Want a dance?

parts.note: to want is to long for
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A sociable party: fancy taking a turn on the floor?
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a long hop is a short-pitched, easily hit delivery, so 'friendly' to the batsman; 'ball' tempts a dance reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket term names a poor, bouncing delivery that is a gift to the batter, hence a kind delivery.

clue.text: Appealing to the general public, united in London area

indicators.note: in places the letter for united inside the district name

parts.note: Poplar is a district in East London
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A unifying message aimed at the masses goes down well in part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: POPLAR is a district of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular means liked by or aimed at ordinary people at large.

clue.text: Roughly fifty, having fizzy lemon in Irish town

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about or roughly
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: fizzy suggests bubbling and agitation, so the letters of lemon are rearranged

explanation.surface: About fifty people are drinking lemonade in a town in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fizzy' rearranges LEMON to ONMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Clonmel is the county town of Tipperary in Ireland.

clue.text: Game American, a stalwart in essence

indicators.note: the essence of the words is what is held within them, so the letters lie inside

explanation.surface: An American playing a game proves essentially a loyal supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in essence' marks the letters hidden across 'American, a stalwart'.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game from Uruguay.

clue.text: Caught by river, fish in basket

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish is caught beside a river and put in a basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is an angler's wicker container for the catch.

clue.text: There's training, after ten, in the Spanish bar

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the Spanish article

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: after places training following ten

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
PE is physical education, training

explanation.surface: Training resumes after ten at a Spanish bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is a verb, to exclude, not a place to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to throw out or ban, which is what barring someone does.

clue.text: Harshly criticise article about superb wonder drug

parts.note: to pan a show is to slate it
ace means excellent
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A critic slates a piece about a so-called miracle cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here just means the article concerns ACE; the pieces run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed cure-all remedy, a miracle medicine.

clue.text: Utter confusion caused by a seaman once church is over

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece that is over others sits above them

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: Pandemonium breaks out when a sailor arrives once the service ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is over' reads as 'has finished', but in a down entry it means placed on top; 'once' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos is complete disorder, a synonym of total confusion.

clue.text: Only fair?

explanation.surface: A sceptical question: is it merely reasonable?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both merely and equitable, two separate senses.

clue.text: Dramatist chooses LP in new compilation

indicators.note: a new compilation puts material together afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A playwright picks a long-player for a fresh compilation album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in new compilation' rearranges CHOOSES plus LP.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles was the Athenian tragedian who wrote Oedipus Rex.

clue.text: It's farewell to the French as one departs a rejected European Union

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters for one departs are turned round

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: Someone bids goodbye to Europe as Brexit-style rejection of the Union happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns I and D (one, departs) round to DI.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for goodbye, literally 'to God', is used in English too.

clue.text: Volatile oils in storage chamber

indicators.note: volatile means unstable and changeable, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Flammable oils are kept in a storage chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volatile' rearranges OILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A silo is a tower or pit for storing grain or silage, or an underground missile chamber.

clue.text: Sort of daily gamble crossing street with female

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the wager goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
a road is a street
she is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman crossing the road places a bet every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' is a noun, a daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsheet is a large-format newspaper, one type of daily paper.
